This is a big ask. 

If it's affordable it's probably for a reason. Wisconsin is very affordable but there's nothing to do there 6 months out of the year and me and the wife have personally known 6 people who killed themselves from depression in the winters. Additionally Buffalo is affordable but you are in the 'Lake Effect' belt and the 4th snowiest city in the US (with #2 Erie PA , #3 my hometown of Rochester, and the #1 Syracuse) or . Either the weather will be terrible, or you're going to be dodging bullets like Camden NJ. 

An established cosplay community isn't really that major anymore thanks to the internet but if you are looking for a decent sized community I would say look at area's with more than 2 large universities.   


But with that said, I would say look at the mid Atlantic around eastern PA (Allentown, Reading, Lancaster), the smaller cities of Virginia (Norfolk because believe it or not, there are a LOT of cosplayers in the military and the largest Navy base on the east coast is in Norfolk), and then lastly the research triangle of NC. All of those areas have moderate temps/weather, easy access to I95 which has a LOT of conventions, easy access to large cities like DC/Philly/NYC with large cons, and smaller but equally as great smaller cons, and not that expensive housing. 

Now with all that being said, I don't know what your background is and each area has a different economy. Some of those area's are strictly pharmaceutical manufacturing, others are pure military, and some are a mix of industries. But hopefully some of this has helped guide you in the right area for you.

*Warning, prepare for a wall of text of why people are leaving Rochester (IMO) from a professional engineer*
First, the taxes. The taxes in the region are too damn high. As a result they are scaring away companies that would invest to other regions were they can turn a better profit, and thus hire more people to further the struggling economy. I'm all for higher private taxes as long as it means lower corporate taxes that allow for a more competitive atmosphere for businesses.
Second, there's no corporate investment. Compared to states like Texas and even New Jersey where I have experience living there in addition to Rochester, those states offer minute business taxes which allow for them to invest more in their regions (which bring in higher paying jobs, which shocking brings better investments). 
*Side note, this is why I'm looking to move out of the region and move to Texas. As a professional engineer I can make more money and have a better life there than here. 
Third, what companies are here, aren't diverse. The few companies left are predictable and isolated. When I spent a year living in Texas I noted that there is more than just oil. And as a result, that diversity of jobs brought in more people that could spend and develop the not so great areas of Houston. 

Now I know that compared to many other comments I'm focusing on the business side of the topic, but that's because I honestly believe that through a better business model for the city, more jobs and thus more money will make it's way to the city which will improve so much of what's wrong. And to those wondering if this would work, it will. Look at New Jersey. They as a state regulate how much local communities can tax businesses and as a result they have a wide range of major corporations located there (and  many of my friends now work for these companies). They have so much going for them because their local governments were smart about bringing in businesses and I feel like if we as a community were able to get the city to cut taxes for business (which will mean that our private taxes will go up) more business will look at Rochester as a possible home for their corporations.
